contract: ../DESIGN.md — Lumen 0.4.60 contract for Windows workspaces and Android reading order. This evidence records HTML design prototypes separately from the live Tauri app.

accessibility.evidence: Prototype review confirmed visible keyboard focus in settings-focus-preview-511x608.jpg, named actions and heading/section structure in the accessibility tree. WCAG relative-luminance calculations from design-tokens.json: light text/surface ratios 13.66:1, 6.91:1, 5.08:1 and primary button 5.10:1; dark ratios 15.83:1, 11.06:1, 8.45:1 and primary button 8.38:1. Android calendar, settings categories, top actions, knowledge submit and memo actions use 48px minimum height in product CSS. Real device, screen-reader and OS accessibility combinations remain unverified.

responsive.evidence: Inspected the interactive HTML prototype at all four target viewport overrides. Desktop today/weekly/calendar use distinct task, date and inspector layouts; mobile reorders the today overview, stacks calendar agenda after the month, makes settings categories sticky and horizontal, and opens secondary navigation as a drawer. The 360px date row was corrected to keep dates on one line. These observations apply to the design preview only; Windows/Tauri and Android WebView rendering remain unverified.

loading.evidence: state-preview.html shows a stable work-area skeleton with aria-busy and a polite loading status; it is a visual contract example, not a live database request.

empty.evidence: state-preview.html distinguishes an empty day and date-aware create action; the demo action only reports that it would not write Lumen data.

error.evidence: state-preview.html presents a specific recoverable error and a retry affordance; the demo retry does not contact Tauri IPC.

partial.evidence: state-preview.html identifies loaded/total counts, exposes a labeled progress bar and a sample continue action; no real pagination is performed.

success.evidence: state-preview.html uses a text status and task summary to demonstrate saved feedback without claiming a database write.

permission.evidence: state-preview.html explains that web completion is not configured and shows the settings next step; the demo action does not navigate or change settings.
